application_review: All 602 baseline source/config hashes were checked before edits and again before registration. Among retained files only the root imports and exact-name verification registry changed; retained proofs, StrongStatement, PNT+ sources and fixed dependency pins remain byte-identical.

The normal-target three-subgroup inclusion is proved by mapping the three subgroups to G/K, applying the retained Hall-Witt three-subgroup equality there, and using the quotient-map kernel K. The target is explicitly normal; no normality of the three source subgroups is assumed or needed.

Induction on the first lower-central index, with the second index generalized, proves [L_i,L_j]<=L_(i+j+1) for the actual mathlib convention L_0=G. The two rotating inclusions use the same induction hypothesis and the exact lower-central successor formula. This strong law was not assumed.

The paper filtration is defined by F_i=L_(i-1), so F_0=F_1=G, F_2=[G,G]. Its antitonicity, normality and all commutator inclusions, including cases with index zero, are derived. The zero-index cases use the proved normality of every actual lower-central layer.

The assumed algebraic Group.IsNilpotent class bound <=s yields F_(s+1)=bot from the retained actual lower-central nilpotency-class theorem; antitonicity proves all later terms trivial. This does not yet construct Group.IsNilpotent from a concrete Lie-group representation.

A continuous commutator map on GxG carries the closure of A x B into the closed target layer. The exact closure-product identity proves that taking topological closure of every layer preserves the full filtered commutator condition.

The closed lower-central filtration is an actual defined sequence, has top layers G, contains the original layers, is closed and normal, and remains terminal in a T1 group. Closure of the trivial subgroup is trivial only with the stated separation hypothesis.

The closed and original filtrations, and hence their cube groups, are proved equal when all original layers are closed. No unconditional equality of an algebraic lower-central layer and its topological closure is claimed.

Existing compact-representative theorems apply to the actual original or closed layers and their restricted lattice. They prove compactness of the cube image and, for the closed series, compactness of the actual cube subgroup modulo its lattice intersection.

Only finitely many layers i<=s require closedness/cocompactness data. Above s the actual layer is bot; its subgroup type and every coset quotient are subsingleton, so compactness is derived without a new geometric hypothesis. The original closed-layer requirement is likewise reduced to i<=s under T1.

The original-law uniform testing theorems now use either the actual lower-central filtration with finite closed-layer inputs, or its closed expansion with no separate closedness input. Abstract filtration, top-layer, terminal-layer and cube compactness assumptions from the earlier theorem are all discharged by these constructions. The restricted-lattice quotients, metric compactness and continuous quotient map remain explicit.

The quotient topology used by the test data is explicitly the topology of the chosen metric, with a uniquely named local instance. Continuity into that topology is an input. Compactness of restricted layer quotients uses their actual subgroup quotient topology; no incompatible topology is silently substituted.

The existing mask models retain their bounds and original all-scale dual estimates. A new canonical closed-lower-central instance proves their uniform nilsequence testing with dimension s+1, without rebuilding the model or changing the root law.

The fixed local paper cube-filtration equations at Section 07 lines 23-32 and the lower-central missing-corner use at lines 117-137 are represented by these actual algebraic filtrations and testing bridges. The rational Lie/lattice assertions in lines 13-22 remain to be proved for concrete nilmanifold data. Ambient quotient compactness alone is not used to assert compactness of every restricted lattice quotient.
